learn.title: Triangles that are not right
learn.body: Right triangles have $\sin$, $\cos$ and $\tan$ ratios. For any triangle, label the angles $A,B,C$ and the sides opposite them $a,b,c$. The law of sines links each side to the sine of its opposite angle.

learn.title: The law
learn.body: $\frac{a}{\sin A}=\frac{b}{\sin B}=\frac{c}{\sin C}$. Use it when you know two angles and a side (ASA or AAS), or two sides and an angle not between them (SSA). You need a matching pair: a side with its opposite angle.
In the SSA case, two different triangles can fit the data. Check whether the second angle $180^\circ-B$ also works.

questions.prompt: Which formula is the law of sines?
questions.explanation: Each side divides by the sine of its opposite angle.

questions.prompt: When is the law of sines the right tool?
choices: Two sides and the angle between them
questions.explanation: Three sides or SAS call for the law of cosines.

questions.prompt: A triangle has $A=50^\circ$ and $B=70^\circ$. What is $C$ in degrees?

questions.explanation: Lowercase side letters match the opposite uppercase angle.

questions.prompt: Match the known data to the law.
questions.explanation: Law of sines needs a side and its opposite angle.

questions.prompt: In a triangle the larger angle faces the:
questions.explanation: In any triangle the longest side is opposite the largest angle.

questions.prompt: Solve for $b$ with the law of sines. Put the steps in order.
steps: Find a known side and its opposite angle
